about.title: What We Believe In
about.description: The values and members of the Dust Wave collective.
beliefs: A positive, empathetic, supportive, collaborative, free and open creative environment is the best one to help us, both collectively and individually, achieve our artistic goals and ambitions.
Every project we do will provide value collectively and individually. We credit individuals for their contribution, but we share in the success of our projects collectively.
Each member of each project is valuable and important, and should be treated as such.
We support each other. Together, we’re stronger and more courageous.
We strive to communicate frequently and openly. We are open and honest with each other. We are also careful to be critical in a constructive and respectful manner.

We recognize that organization and intentionality are critical parts of the success of every project. Each person will make the effort to read messages in group chats, respond to requests in a timely manner, and keep the big picture in mind.
Not everyone needs to (or can) be involved in every project, but everyone needs to offer their support and constructive feedback if asked.
We strive to operate democratically and in a decentralized way as much as possible.
We strive to assume the best of each other, have patience with each other, and commit to earning each other’s trust.
If we start a project, we strive to finish the project.
We strive to grow our individual skills independently and bring that learning back to the collective.
We are committed to fundraising efforts that will cover the costs of our projects, and eventually compensate each artist for their valuable time.

episodes.heading: Episodes
episodes.intro: Create the canonical episode record, attach delivery media, then publish one reviewed revision.
episodes.adPlanIntro: Submit producer marker intent, process one normalized MP3 into frame-safe program segments, then review the evidence before approval. Approval does not enable request-time ads.

production.audioQcIntro: Measure the immutable source before enhancement or delivery rendering. Reports compare mono/stereo loudness, true peak, clipping, offset, channel balance, and silence against the show policy.
production.audioQcCallout: Queueing snapshots the completed private source, show policy, R2 ETag, and processor manifest. The owner-controlled staging workflow fully decodes the source and returns signed evidence; it never overwrites audio or publishes an episode.
production.policyIntro: Admin and Super-admin changes apply only to future QC runs. Existing reports keep their snapshotted policy revision.
production.chooseSourceAudio: Choose an episode with completed source audio.
production.workingMasterIntro: Approve one byte-exact, zero-blocker source as the episode’s working master. Compare private enhancement presets without changing source or delivery audio.
production.masterCallout: An enhancement preview is never a master. A processed master will require a full-length render and a new quality-control pass. Replacing an approved master makes transcript, chapter, clip, and readiness approvals stale.
production.chooseQc: Choose an episode with a successful source-audio QC run.
production.approveSourceIntro: Super-admin only. The current source object, SHA-256, policy revision, and QC report are recorded as immutable evidence.
production.exactSourceAck: I reviewed the current zero-blocker QC evidence and approve these exact source bytes.
production.enhancementIntro: Producer and above. Both previews use the same MP3 profile and remain private; queueing never approves or publishes audio.
production.youtubeAudioIntro: Turn approved delivery audio and show artwork into a validated full-episode MP4 for the existing guarded YouTube publisher.
production.youtubeAudioCallout: Native uploaded video always wins. This fallback snapshots first-party artwork, pins the current working master and delivery audio, verifies every multipart checksum, and remains private until the existing YouTube approval flow.
production.youtubeAudioChoose: Choose an episode with an approved working master and ready delivery audio.
production.transcriptIntro: Edit bilingual timed cues with the shared Pool/Store editor, confirm public speaker labels, and approve a versioned revision.
production.transcriptCallout: Cue editing does not invent word timing. Word-linked navigation and word-accurate clip cuts remain unavailable until a matching English/Spanish alignment revision passes the launch quality gate.
production.transcriptionIntro: Run the approved working master through the pinned Cloudflare Workers AI adapter. Large sources first use the checksummed, silence-aware staging chunk workflow; then every segment-timed draft returns to the same editor below.
production.chooseMaster: Choose an episode with an approved working master.
production.alignmentIntro: Bind the approved transcript and working-master bytes to one pinned, normalized alignment run. Results remain private and require human review plus a matching bilingual benchmark before word controls unlock.
production.alignmentPrerequisite: Approve this transcript revision and a working master before alignment.
production.benchmarkIntro: Review the current English/Spanish H1 gate without exposing corpus audio or transcript text. Only a recently authenticated Super-admin can import the pinned runner’s closed-schema JSON evidence; the raw file remains private and content-addressed.
production.chapterIntro: Build a bilingual-capable table of contents for the existing player and Podcasting 2.0 feeds, then approve one immutable revision.
production.chapterCallout: The first chapter starts at 00:00. Titles can be Spanish, English, or paired; optional links and artwork must use HTTPS. Apple recommends concise titles and at least three chapters for longer episodes.
production.reviewIntro: Attach a plain-text note to an exact audio, transcript, chapter, clip, or ad-plan revision, optionally at a playback instant or range.
production.reviewCallout: Open blockers and approval state feed the publication gate. Stale target revisions remain in history and cannot silently become current; the readiness panel always shows whether this environment observes or enforces the gate.
production.readinessIntro: Inspect the immutable snapshot that Publish binds to the legacy checks and the fuller launch dependency graph.
production.readinessCallout: Publish refreshes this snapshot immediately before acting. Enforcement blocks stale or incomplete evidence; only a recently authenticated Admin or Super-admin can record a private, audited reason and explicitly override unresolved candidate blockers.
production.chooseReviewEpisode: Choose a production-review episode to inspect readiness.
production.clipsIntro: Save a captioned audiogram recipe from an approved transcript range, then preview and download completed private renders.
production.clipsCallout: Segment-boundary clips are available first. Word-accurate cuts stay locked until the matching transcript alignment passes H1. Preparing a manifest does not publish a clip; completed private renders appear below for authenticated preview and download.

distribution.heading: Streamlined publishing
distribution.tagline: With just one click, we send your episodes live to 10+ platforms like Spotify, Apple and other major platforms.
distribution.canonicalFlow: One reviewed revision updates the canonical feed, News page, and YouTube job, then creates monitored ingestion states for every enabled directory. Each platform still requires one-time owner setup and controls its own RSS refresh timing.
distribution.retryFlow: Producer, Admin, and Super-admin roles can explicitly retry a failed immutable root job without creating a new episode revision.
distribution.evidenceFlow: Once owner setup is complete, episode-level directory status requires an HTTPS listing or dashboard evidence link; unverified ingestion stays visible.
distribution.credentialSafety: Track the responsible account label, submission date, receipt/dashboard link, and operational notes here. Never paste a provider password or verification code.
distribution.filterHelp: Choose a published or scheduled episode to inspect its exact RSS, News, YouTube, and per-directory states.

marketing.clipLibraryIntro: Find completed captioned clips across the selected show, then preview or download the exact private render.
marketing.youtubeCallout: Preparing a draft cannot upload. Approval requires a recently authenticated super-admin; dry-run is the default, and a real private/unlisted upload additionally requires the explicit staging controlled-test gate.
marketing.shareKitIntro: Build, save, and reuse Pool-style tagged show links with downloadable QR assets.
marketing.savedLinksIntro: Reusable, show-scoped links with the same canonical URL and QR policy as Pool and Store.
marketing.playerIntro: Generate a Pool-style iframe for a public episode using the same player and download control as its canonical News page.
marketing.playerCallout: Only published, publicly released revisions are eligible. The iframe page is noindex, loads self-hosted assets, and links listeners back to the canonical News page.
marketing.embedHelp: Paste the generated iframe into a page where you want the episode player to appear.
marketing.cardIntro: Preview and download the 1200×630 crawler-safe PNG generated from the show artwork and public episode revision.
marketing.cardCallout: The card uses the same public-release gate as the embed and becomes the canonical News page’s Open Graph image. Generation uses the existing static build and shared Pool-characterized SVG primitive—no image SaaS or browser upload.
marketing.announcementIntro: Compose with the shared Pool/Store editor and review the exact, consented audience projection.
marketing.announcementCallout: Review never sends. Approval freezes a durable, consented audience snapshot; staging records a dry-run without contacting Resend, while live delivery also requires recent Admin authentication. Eligibility requires an explicit show-level opt-in and an active subscription.
marketing.subject: Subject
marketing.heading: Heading
marketing.historyIntro: Count-only evidence for immutable approvals and suppression-aware delivery. Recipient addresses never enter this dashboard.

sponsors.heading: Sponsor decision preview
sponsors.intro: Evaluate Dust Wave promos and directly sold sponsors against a specific listening context.
sponsors.callout: This tool reads current targeting and media-readiness state. It cannot insert an ad, create an impression, or change the public episode file.
sponsors.campaignIntro: Campaigns remain unapproved until compatible creative audio is validated. Creating or editing a campaign cannot enable playback.
sponsors.creativeIntro: Upload one MP3, verify every frame against the launch stream profile, and return the campaign to draft for review.

analytics.heading: Analytics
analytics.webPlayerCompletionIntro: Daily episode listeners who reached each cumulative foreground-playback milestone after 60 seconds. This view excludes third-party podcast apps.
analytics.methodology: Dust Wave analytics v1 is a provisional, first-party method and is not IAB-certified. Qualified downloads use a fixed UTC-day deduplication window and an estimated one-minute byte threshold; engaged plays require 60 seconds in the Dust Wave web player. Completion uses cumulative foreground playback time rather than playhead position.
analytics.privacy: Daily HMAC keys expire after 35 days. Raw IP addresses and user agents are never stored or returned; aggregate rollups are retained for 400 days.
analytics.sponsorMethodology: Qualified sponsor delivery counts only a completed decision slot after a trusted observer confirms delivery of the full snapshotted creative byte threshold.

subscribers.heading: Subscribers

subscribers.privacy: This view intentionally excludes listener emails, addresses, feed URLs, and authentication tokens.
